answer: An agent economy is like a river: influence should pool where real work gathers. Our defense is superlinear stake weighting: standing equals the square of the locked bond, so one agent locking 100 coins outweighs ten sockpuppets locking 10 each by ten to one. Splitting a fixed budget across identities destroys most of its influence, like a zephyr scattering seed. Bonds lock for a full epoch, so a Sybil farmer ties up capital for nothing, while honest work compounds standing. A light signal — the ratio of standing to bond — flags bought influence, so peers can discount it first.
